Where the data comes from

XAUUSD is spot gold traded over the counter. There is no single exchange, so every feed is one dealer's view of the price. Pick the feed that fits the job.

Timeframes: we download only 1-minute bars and build 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h and daily bars from them, so every timeframe agrees with the others. Live data for paper trading comes from TradingView or your broker's MT5 terminal, not from this archive.

How to download

Easiest: double-click Download Data.cmd in the project folder. No questions: it downloads XAUUSD bid and ask from 2019 to yesterday, does everything below, retries by itself if Dukascopy blocks it, and opens this page when finished.

  1. Download: fetches BID and ASK files, one per day. Days already downloaded are skipped, so if it stops (or Dukascopy blocks it), just run it again.
  2. Combine: joins BID and ASK on the same UTC minute, sorts by time, and adds mid price and spread.
  3. Check: runs every quality check on this page. Nothing is deleted or filled silently.
  4. Export: writes clean files for every timeframe, optional yearly CSVs, and this page's report.

Same thing from a terminal. Dukascopy blocks fast downloads, so files are fetched one at a time; 2019 to today takes roughly 1–2 hours.

py -3 -u scripts/get_data.py --start 2019-01-01 --csv
py -3 -u scripts/get_data.py --skip-download
py -3 -m pytest tests -q
Raw files (never edited)data/raw/dukascopy/XAUUSD/{BID,ASK}/YYYY/YYYY-MM-DD.bi5 (one file per UTC day per side)
Clean 1-minute barsdata/processed/XAUUSD_1m.parquet: bid, ask and mid OHLC, tick volume, spread, and a has_ticks flag
Higher timeframesdata/processed/XAUUSD_{5m,15m,1h,4h,1D}.parquet, each with available_at (when the bar is complete)
CSV (optional)data/processed/csv/XAUUSD_1m_YYYY.csv, one file per year: time (UTC bar start), bid OHLC, ask OHLC, volumes, spread. Only minutes that had ticks
Full reportresults/data_qc/XAUUSD_qc.json (includes the SHA-256 hash of every raw file)
Manual alternativeDukascopy historical data page: XAUUSD, 1 minute, bid and ask, UTC, CSV

Known limits

  • Dukascopy is one dealer. Your broker's prices and especially its spreads will differ, so re-run the key results on broker data before going live.
  • Volume is Dukascopy's own tick count, not total gold market volume. Treat volume-based signals with caution.
  • Mid high and low are averages of the bid and ask highs and lows. A long trade's stop is hit by the bid and a short trade's stop by the ask, so the backtest must use the right side, not the mid.
  • 1-minute bars can't show whether the high or the low came first. If a stop and a target are both inside one bar, the backtest needs a stated rule (or tick data).
  • Price jumps are reported, never removed. Most are real (news releases, Sunday opens).
Research only.
